items.evidence: "The part" cannot resolve to parent_collection C1 (Prov.1.1-Prov.9.18, which runs well past 4.27); it only resolves to writer_part p02 (Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27, per SP/Prov/writer/p02_rows.jsonl), a campaign scratch-tiling artifact, not a literary unit. book_strategy Prov.md Sec.8 REGISTER PURGE / TOOLKIT.md Standing rules bar "file-order talk...in row prose EVER" and "positional row references"; using the writer_part boundary as the counting frame for an ordinal claim in row prose is exactly that. items.claim: 5.1-5.6 is a clean instruction_lecture bounded by the singular beni vocative at 5.1 and the plural banim vocative reopening at 5.7, correctly disqualifying the 5.4 "two-edged sword" as a WEB-only numeral rather than a Hebrew count.
items.evidence: collate.py returns byte tier for all three quoted Hebrew runs (oshb:Prov.5.1, oshb:Prov.5.4, oshb:Prov.5.6). prov_device_inventory.json bni_address confirms Prov.5.1 is one of the 22 word-bound vocative verses, while Prov.5.7's banim form appears in neither bni_address nor bene_construct, so the singular/plural contrast the row argues is byte-real. The row pre-empts the TOOLKIT's own "two-edged sword" hazard by naming kherev piyyot (sword of edges) as the Hebrew and labeling the WEB "two" a rendering choice. pmarks_Prov.json shows the only span-adjacent mark is the Prov.5.6 petuchah, correctly disclosed as the span's own close; no paseq or K/Q note falls inside Prov.5.1-Prov.5.6.

items.claim: The 5.20-5.23 boundary argument omits a paseq inside its own span and does not disclose a root-level wordplay tying its opening verb back across the very seam it calls a "reopening."
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json paseq inventory shows Prov.5.21=1, a paseq inside the row's own Prov.5.20-Prov.5.23 span that is nowhere disclosed, though the row does disclose the adjoining Prov.5.23 petuchah -- a mark-disclosure-symmetry gap (TOOLKIT.md: "UNCONDITIONAL span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry" applies to every disclosure object, not only petuchah). Separately, byte inspection of verse_map_oshb.json shows the root shagah ("be captivated/go astray") recurring three times across the row's own front seam and span: תִּשְׁגֶּ֥ה closes Prov.5.19 (the immediately preceding, non-assigned verse; WEB "Be captivated always with her love"), תִשְׁגֶּ֣ה opens the row's own Prov.5.20 third word (WEB "why should you...be captivated"), and יִשְׁגֶּֽה closes the row's own Prov.5.23. The WEB rendering itself preserves the pun ("captivated"/"captivated"), so this is not a translation-only artifact. The row's "reopens direct address" framing treats Prov.5.20 as a clean restart and does not disclose or argue around this byte-true device straddling its own seam, which TOOLKIT.md's cross-seam-cohesion rule requires ("a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed").

items.claim: The 6.6-6.11 rationale does not disclose that its own closing participle shares the root halak with the participle opening the following unit at 6.12, a byte-true device invisible in the WEB rendering the row's argument leans on.
items.evidence: Byte inspection of verse_map_oshb.json: Prov.6.11 closes "...u-va כִמְהַלֵּ֥ךְ..." -- the word כִמְהַלֵּ֥ךְ (WEB "as a robber") -- and Prov.6.12 opens "...ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ..." (WEB "is he who walks") right after its nominal subject. Both are participial forms of the same root halak, straddling the row's own back seam. WEB's "robber" for 6.11 obscures the root the row's own contrast ("second-person imperative...distinct from the third-person participial portrait that opens at 6.12") does not address. TOOLKIT.md's cross-seam-cohesion rule requires this be disclosed or argued around; it is neither. The mark layer itself is handled correctly (petuchah at Prov.6.11 own-close and Prov.6.5 adjoining; paseq at Prov.6.9 and Prov.6.10 both disclosed) -- the gap is specifically this undisclosed root recurrence.
tier_citations: verse_map_web.json:Prov.6.11="as a robber" (root obscured in translation)

items.claim: 6.12-6.15 is a clean proverb_cluster on the shared-subject participial portrait, correctly disclosing the 6.14 K/Q pair's specific spelling, its own paseq, and both bracketing petuchahs.
items.evidence: collate.py returns byte tier for both quoted Hebrew runs (oshb:Prov.6.12, oshb:Prov.6.15). verse_map_oshb.json Prov.6.14 literally reads the inline ketiv מדנים immediately followed by the pointed qere מִדְיָנִ֥ים -- byte-confirming the row's specific ketiv/qere spelling claim, not merely its presence (pmarks_Prov.json kq:Prov.6.14=1). pmarks_Prov.json paseq:Prov.6.14=1 is disclosed, and the petuchahs at Prov.6.15 (own close) and Prov.6.11 (adjoining) are both correctly labeled.
